steps.text: Central District
A short while before

options: How are you certain Amiya's group will reach the command tower...
...without crossing one of Talulah's elite squads?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is the problem with conspirators.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Take a warlord, or a tyrant of a devious king. Their strongholds are always easy to defend, hard to attack.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They know their own deeds will invite furious retribution without fail. They'll use superior strength and advanced armaments to deploy unyielding defense.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yet, seeing as Talulah's despotic behavior is confirmed to be some kind of act, she would not do things this way.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Experience, theory, phenomena.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have no confidence. I can only derive the facts.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Truthfully, I'm hoping to see you ever offer your own opinion.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Or maybe you're already content with silence as a brand of opinion?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Then I thank you for your understanding.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If my thought process was one that won your approval...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Did you think that I would thus feel some kind of happy?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Respect is a two-way street. If you value my point of view, and arrive at any useful conclusions, then I in turn will give your point of view serious consideration.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Talulah is maintaining her own image. She needs to have the normal Infected respect her, have the Sarkaz mercenaries obey her, have the guerrillas trust her, have the zealots worship her...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She needs to have the distance between her and them clearly visible, and have these people able to examine each other.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: According to a series of behavior exhibited by Reunion so far, we can very clearly realize that Reunion's other leaders do not particularly recognize Talulah's conduct at all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even Patriot, seeing through to her scheme, had no power to reverse the tide in the middle of its change. If he could have killed Talulah, all the same, he still would have been unable to alter Reunion tending towards collapse.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To say nothing of the plot to exploit the Infected that Talulah has drawn up inside her own head... The time she would need likely far exceed the time Reunion has existed so far.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I conjecture that all of Reunion's actions up to now have been premised on a plan. Namely...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: 'Reunion will perish after all this is over.'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Talulah will scatter keen, hidden forces across every part of her territory. When she needs them, she'll assemble them, and have them make their appearance at the right moment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I believe the Empire of Ursus's Third Army would not permit any Infected to act freely whatsoever.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: However, Reunion's current conduct is all within the bounds of their tolerance. Superficial violence, lacking discipline and organization. The Third Army must be happy to see it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Think about it carefully. Would they limit themselves to being onlookers? Thus, would they risk truly, willingly letting Talulah control a whole city—even a whole country's state of affairs?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Or perhaps, even this is one of the weights on Talulah's scales, used to swindle the Ursus military out of their power... having them hibernate somewhere, waiting until the situation is just about to move on from her control.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And then, in the truest sense, she'll be able to use... the power she could never even touch. Just as she wishes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But that needs time.

options: Now that you say all that, how is she not a tyrant?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Because while current Reunion wants that in a leader, it doesn't truly need that in a leader.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A tyrant treasures one's own enablers, even if a tyrant more often than not recklessly destroys them for lack of foresight or composure, and weeps truest, deepest tears for it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A conspirator does not. The tyrant has chess pieces, and the conspirator does too; but the tyrant is with them on the chessboard, while the conspirator sits outside of it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We can suppose she has humanity, and thus might make mistakes. But if we're talking about a qualified conspirator with a scheme on the tracks, then even if she herself died, her scheme would continue as a matter of course.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If they were, we'd hardly be taking Rhodes Island's operators to hell and back.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The only thing naturally useless is killing her. So, in every part and every place, we must break down her plot, antagonize her instructions, and lead her scheme to failure.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If we cannot halt a landship's forward march, then we will tear it to pieces, and make it arrive at its destination no more than an empty carapace.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Ah, maybe I shouldn't have put it to you like that. Don't get me wrong, we still need to stop this Chernobog core city.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, you've worried about whether or not Amiya's group will run into any incidents...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I think what's on show before us is the real incident, here.

steps.name: Herdified Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: W, W. Where W? W stronger.

steps.name: Herdified Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Don't, don't enter...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: (A certain Sarkaz tribe's language)

steps.name: Herdified Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Underground full of darkness. Darkness create evil. Evil bring pain.

steps.name: Herdified Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Too much, pain.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: (A certain Sarkaz tribe's language)

steps.name: Herdified Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Will you, share our pain?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No luck. Even if they weren't born in Kazdel, they should still have some kind of reaction to a hint of their native language. Their ability to actively think has been damaged.

options: Could those words you were saying have any effect on them?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They were meant to in the first place.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No, wait... this wasn't a common-sense idea. Don't get excited.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But if not even this lets me rouse their conscious, then they've already lost all capacity for thought, beyond simply their ability to express.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It means their brain's activity has been sealed off, or that their nervous system has been perturbed by the infected organs... either way, we don't have enough time left to ascertain the true answer.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just based on what facts we have, it's not looking good.

options: They don't seem like they'll attack us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They're preventing us from entering. Deeply infected Sarkaz mercenaries in this area number around six, and seem to spend most of their time set to an unconscious roam.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Their range of movement doesn't extend outside this passage. These severely Infected collected here only after they picked up on our activity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Moreover, as long as we don't cross some boundary, they don't do anything further.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Reconnaissance operator. Can you detect our straight-line distance to the Sarcophagus? Determine position via the waveform I provided.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...1.4km. Precise figure?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...If my calculations aren't wrong, then the breakout of conflict between Reunion and Sarkaz special Infected happened to be roughly at distance 1.4km from the City Hall too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We initially planned to enter the Sarcophagus holding from the City Hall basement shelter passage, but as things are, that exit's likely been occupied by Sarkaz special Infected of the same kind.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have an unconfirmed conjecture, Doctor...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We don't know what their goal is, but these Sarkaz special Infected are likely preventing anyone else from entering the sarcophagus holding, and by happy coincidence, this district they've controlled measures 1.4km out.

options: You might be right, but what about their goal, then?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: (Shakes her head)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: At the very least, it's not the same goal these Sarkaz originally had.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Poor Sarkaz, hailing from Kazdel. No matter where, they still become tools.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I believe there are similarities between the Infected and the Sarkaz's current situations. These Sarkaz here with us could only choose to well with hate, or to lose it all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Things were meant to have changed. We have that power.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Those Teekaz who lost their homeland—have become Sarkaz, rootless as people.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And now, the Sarkaz before us can barely even be called people.

options: How do you want to do things?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: All operators, inspect your hazmat equipment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What we're facing may be a Class II Emergency Infective situation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, in minimizing wear and tear to the utmost, we must halt the special Infected's activity to the utmost.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...We haven't stepped in to resolve an Emergency Infective state for a while. This outfit looks entirely like Ursus's Infected Patrol Unit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There's something I can't deny—the hazmat equipment we've been provided with is emblematic of Ursus's cruel rule over the Infected... it shares the same prototypical design.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Though our approach is intrinsically distinct from the Infected Patrol Unit, I can only hope we're able to continue preserving that intrinsic difference—that outside forces don't force us to change beyond recognition.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The same hope we hold for so many things. Just like I told you about some time before. I hope you'll hope so too.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ————Was—Madame Ch'en here?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Which way was he headed?

steps.name: Shadow Guard
steps.text: West. Stone's throw from the exclusion zone of Glowing Hoof.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...He plotted all of this. It was to ensure the area where we signed the pact was secure. Leithanien expanded their contended exclusion zone, overlapping our own.

steps.name: Shadow Guard
steps.text: We can infiltrate, kill Kashchey and bring back the Miss.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: No. He's already prepared.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...In this meeting, the Twin Empresses directly dispatched the Empresses' Voice, and they weren't short of armed forces.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: The Empresses are fresh upon the throne. If Kashchey intends to blow our diplomacy apart, all our transgressive conduct may very well be the Empresses' excuse to flaunt their power.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: We can't give Kashchey more opportunities to harm Lungmen, or even Yan.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: Uncle!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hui-chieh...

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: Uncle... it's not Tal's fault!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I'm not blaming her.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: ...Then you should get mad at me.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You haven't done anything wrong.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: I told her I was gonna go with her. But then I got scared... I... let go of her hand. I didn't go with her...

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: She looked... really scared. I was really scared, and she was too. I... I did something wrong.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...Hui-chieh, she made the mistake, not you.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: Huh? B-but you said you wouldn't blame her, Uncle!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: No, I won't.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: But didn't... didn't she do something wrong? If she does something wrong, you're... not gonna get mad at her?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: She doesn't know the truth. It's not a truth anyone should be privy to, so of course she'd make a mistake. If not now, she would in the future.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...In so many cases, the wrong thing shouldn't be punished. Not only do we make mistakes, we'll make so many of them. If there's some mistake, we will make it. We can't dodge that, nor escape it.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Talulah simply made the mistake she was bound to.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: Is that still doing something wrong, then?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Yes, of course it is. This world of ours wouldn't forgive something just because it was bound to happen.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: The world is harsh, the people are harsh, the regimes are harsh. Apart from right and wrong, they don't care a damn. As if it's right and wrong keeping them alive, and not what they breathe and swallow...!

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: I don't get what you're saying, Uncle.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: Does... does it mean Tal can still come back?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: —I don't know, Hui-chieh. I don't know.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: ...*sob*... Is it because of me... Tal won't come back? It's my fault... it's my fault... Tal...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hui-chieh!

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: *whimper*...!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Wipe your tears away.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Or cry, then. I'll give you five minutes. After you're done crying, if there's not still tears in your eyes, I'll tell you what you should do.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: ...Waaah...! Tal...!
Wei Yenwu gazes towards the sky. He considers bending down to comfort the tiny girl, but after hesitating, feels as if he isn't suited to the task.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You're done crying, then.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: ...Mm-hm. I want Tal back. What should I do?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I'll teach you a world of things. I'll teach you how to supervise a city, how to fend off villains, how to treat your friends.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Do as I say, and Talulah will have a chance of coming back.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: Wh-what do I do? Will Tal be able to come back, really? Are you tricking me, Uncle?

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: ...Mama... Mama said, you only know howta trick people. Can... can I really believe you?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I've made a massive mistake of my own, and it led to your mother despising me for her whole life. Even on her deathbed, she couldn't have let go. What she told you is understandable.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: But mistakes can be made right.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hui-chieh, listen carefully. Proper conduct is worth striving your whole life for. Correcting a mistake is worth putting life itself at stake for.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Talulah's departure was a mistake. Every consequence it brings, I will bear.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: And you, Hui-chieh. You'd better grow up fast.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: What'll it be like when I grow up?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hmm. When you grow up... you'll be able to change everything.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Perhaps. Or let's put it this way: so long as you believe, it will be real.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I'll teach you to wield a sword, Hui-chieh.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: To wield Chi Xiao.
'As move unsheathing blade, cleave now as cleft.'
